verses.text: So think of us as Christ’s servants, trusted to manage God’s hidden truths.
What matters for a manager is being found faithful.
But your opinion—or any human court’s verdict—is a small thing to me. I don’t even sit in judgment over myself.
My conscience doesn’t accuse me, but that doesn’t automatically make me right. The Lord is the one who judges me.

So don’t hand down a verdict before the time. Wait until the Lord comes; he’ll bring hidden darkness into the light and uncover what hearts are really planning. Then each person will get praise from God.
Family, I used myself and Apollos as examples for your sake. Learn not to go beyond what’s written, and don’t get puffed up, choosing one person over another.
Who made you so different from everybody else? What do you have that you didn’t receive? And if you received it, why flex like you got it yourself?
“You’re already full? Rich already? You started ruling without us? I wish you really were ruling—then we could rule with you too!”
I think God has put us apostles on display last of all, like people sentenced to die. We’ve become a spectacle for the whole world—for angels and people alike.
We look foolish for Christ, while you’re the wise ones in Christ. We’re weak, but you’re strong; you’re honored, while we get disrespected.
Right up to this moment, we’re hungry, thirsty, poorly dressed, beaten up, and without a stable home.
We work hard with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless them. When they persecute us, we hang in there.
When they slander us, we answer with kindness. We’ve become the world’s trash—the dirt everybody wipes away—even now.
I’m not writing this to embarrass you. I’m correcting you like my beloved children.
You might have ten thousand tutors in Christ, but you don’t have many spiritual fathers. In Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.
So I’m asking you: follow my example.
That’s why I sent Timothy, my dear and faithful child in the Lord. He’ll remind you how I live in Christ, the same way I teach everywhere in every church.
Some of you are acting all puffed up, like I’m never coming back.
But I’ll visit soon, if the Lord wills. Then I’ll find out whether these big talkers have real power or just words.
God’s Kingdom isn’t talk. It’s power.
So what do you want? Should I show up with a rod, or with love and a gentle spirit?
